Paste or edit the JSON you want to test

Run the case to see the parsed result preview.
Run this first after installing on a device to confirm all built-in cases still pass.
Paste a real API response, choose an entry point, target type, and policy, then compare SafeParser with native Gson.
Run every default case once. Use this page first to confirm the demo app and parser features are healthy.
Paste your own API response and compare SafeParser with native Gson.
Verify object fallback, primitives, collections, maps, object number policy, and compatibility behavior.
Verify public APIs, Kotlin APIs, presets, GsonBuilder passthrough, annotations, and safe fallback behavior.
Verify events, contract reports, observer failure isolation, and low-level event bridging.
Verify empty responses, raw JSON capture, observer isolation, and converter delegation in Retrofit.
No uncaught demo runtime exception. Scenario-captured exceptions are shown in parsed output.
Run the case to see output.
Tap “Run full check”. All default cases are expected to pass.
This page does not need case selection or JSON input.
This feature page has no fixed cases.
Quick check only shows a summary. Switch to a feature page to inspect one case.
All demo cases pass and the detailed self-check report is copied.
Detailed events are shown inside each case block in the parsed output.
Detailed self-check report copied. Failed cases: %1$d

Many demo model fields in DemoModels.kt define default values. When SafeParser falls back, the parsed JSON shows the concrete default fields, so a short expectation such as User() means id=0 and name=anonymous.
SafeParser should handle this malformed or edge-case JSON without crashing the demo app. Inspect the parsed output and event stream to decide whether the fallback value matches your project.
Sample JSON has been written into the shared input box. You can edit it before verifying. Target type: %1$s
Edit the JSON and tap “Verify JSON”. The page compares SafeParser with native Gson.
Calls GsonSafeParser.fromJson directly. Use this when your app integrates through Gson itself.
Runs through GsonSafeConverterFactory. Use this when your app receives the JSON from Retrofit.
A common response wrapper with code and non-null data object. Good for testing data=[] or data=null.
A response wrapper whose data field can be null. Good for low-interference or NullOnly policies.
A root list of users. Good for checking whether bad list items can be skipped safely.
Contains List, Set, Map, and number lists. Good for collection shape mismatches and item skipping.
Collections and maps are nullable. Good for comparing null fallback with empty collection fallback.
Contains Int, Long, BigDecimal, Boolean, and String. Good for primitive type mismatches.
Contains an object field and strongly typed Map. Good for map key/value parsing and partial skipping.
Contains Int-key maps and nested maps. Good for bad key skipping and map item event attribution.
Contains Any and Map<String, Any>. Good for observing object number strategies and dynamic fields.
Contains EnumSet and EnumMap. Good for checking enum container construction in a real app.
Contains JSONObject and JSONArray. Good for checking org.json adapters.
Uses the SafeParser 1.0.4 default config. Start here to observe mismatch evidence and default return boundaries.
Returns null for many mismatched fields and delegates primitives to Gson, staying closer to native Gson.
Captures raw JSON with mismatch events. Useful while debugging backend contract problems.
Primitive adapters are delegated to native Gson. Useful for checking which primitive errors resurface.
Uses Gson LONG_OR_DOUBLE for Any/Object numbers. Useful for dynamic field number expectations.
Explicitly enables object and collection shape coercion. Useful for checking object fields returned as arrays and collection fields returned as objects.
Enables raw JSON capture with a 10-byte limit. Useful for checking log truncation behavior.
